newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast gasoline firms with NYMEX unleaded.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast gasoline firms with NYMEX unleaded.

text.p: U.S. West Coast gasoline prices firmed in reaction to a rise in unleaded gasoline futures, while distillates idled in slow talk, traders said.
Local trade remained sluggish following a two-day industry conference late last week, brokers said.

Meanwhile, NYMEX gasoline strengthened on rumors Amoco sought spot gasoline barrels in the U.S. Gulf Coast market. The company shut a fluid catalytic cracker at its large Texas City, Texas, refinery Monday, regulators said.
NYMEX gasoline settled 0.20 cent higher, but rose as much as 1.65 cents a gallon to 71.75 cents a gallon Monday.
Locally, an industry source said Ultramar shut a 12,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) coker at its Los Angeles-area plant.
The shutdown came amid rumors West Coast refiners would cut production due to poor profits.
Spot prices for Los Angeles conventional unleaded gasoline rose 0.50 - 0.75 cent a galllon early, ranging 63 to 64 cents a gallon. Premium grade stood five cents higher.
CARB-grade conventional gasoline rose 0.50 to 1.00 cents a gallon to 67.50/69 cents.
Bids for low sulphur diesel and jet fuel rose a cent, leaving both grades 71/72 cents a gallon.
